answer: Every epoch, a few randomly drawn relay agents act as a beacon, each pinging every identity at an unannounced moment. Those round-trip times weave a latency thread that roughly triangulates where a key's hardware sits. Fifty sybils docked at one wharf, a single server, return near-identical fingerprints and get merged into one reward seat. To pass, an attacker must rent a separate machine in a distinct region per fake key (assume ~$20/month each, a design assumption), and that host can't be pooled across clones without collapsing them back into one.
